title: Write the strategy as a short narrative
summary: A short written narrative explains the strategy better than slides. It forces clear thinking and lets people read, question and remember it.

beginner: Write no more than two pages in plain sentences.
Cover the diagnosis, the bets, what you won't do and how you will measure progress.
Use one real example to make it concrete.
Ask someone outside the team to read it and tell it back to you.
intermediate: Tie every bet back to the diagnosis.
Answer the obvious objections in the text.
Run a reading session where people read first, then discuss.
experienced: Write a version for the board and one for teams, with the same core.
Remove fluff and buzzwords that hide weak thinking.
Make the narrative the reference for later decisions.

toolExamples.google-docs: Write the narrative and collect comments in one document.
toolExamples.confluence: Publish the final narrative as the strategy's home page.

definitionOfDone: Narrative of two pages or fewer
pitfalls: Slides with bullet points instead of an argument
